ok.de: Richtig: tomorrow = mögliche Zukunft → if + Präsens (rains). will steht nur im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: tomorrow = possible future → if + present (rains). will appears only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach if steht kein will: Der if-Teil nimmt das Präsens (rains).
wrong.en: No will after if: the if-clause takes the present (rains).

wrong.de: would gehört in den Hauptsatz einer Annahme. Regen morgen ist aber wirklich möglich.
wrong.en: would belongs in the main clause of an assumption. Rain tomorrow is a real possibility.

wrong.de: Das Past macht es zur Annahme. Aber tomorrow nennt eine echte Möglichkeit.
wrong.en: The past makes it an assumption. But tomorrow names a real possibility.

wrong.de: Mit it braucht das Präsens ein -s: it rains.
wrong.en: With it the present needs an -s: it rains.

ok.de: Richtig: would travel = Annahme → im if-Teil das Past: had.
ok.en: Right: would travel = assumption → the if-clause takes the past: had.

wrong.de: have ist Präsens und würde zu will travel passen. would travel verlangt das Past.
wrong.en: have is present and would fit will travel. would travel calls for the past.

wrong.de: would steht nicht im if-Teil. Dort braucht die Annahme das Past (had).
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The assumption needs the past (had) there.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht in den if-Teil, und would travel verlangt das Past.
wrong.en: will does not go in the if-clause, and would travel calls for the past.

ok.de: Richtig: had left ist vorbei → would not have + 3. Form: wouldn't have missed.
ok.en: Right: had left (over) → would not have + participle: wouldn't have missed.

wrong.de: Nach would have steht die 3. Form: would not have missed.
wrong.en: After would have comes the participle: would not have missed.

wrong.de: Nach had left liegt die Folge in der Vergangenheit: would not have missed.
wrong.en: After had left the result lies in the past: would not have missed.

wrong.de: will passt nicht: Der Zug ist schon weg, die Folge liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: will does not fit: the train is gone, the result lies in the past.

wrong.de: Die Folge braucht would not have + 3. Form, keine einfache Zeitform.
wrong.en: The result needs would not have + participle, not a simple tense.

ok.de: Richtig: reale Bedingung → if + Präsens (accepts). Im Hauptsatz steht will.
ok.en: Right: real condition → if + present (accepts). The main clause takes will.

wrong.de: would steht nicht im if-Teil. Die Bedingung bis Freitag ist realistisch: Präsens.
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The condition by Friday is realistic: present.

wrong.de: Das Past macht es zur Annahme. Hier ist es ein realer Fall mit will im Hauptsatz.
wrong.en: The past makes it an assumption. Here it is a real case with will in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach if steht kein will: Der if-Teil nimmt das Präsens, will steht im Hauptsatz.
wrong.en: No will after if: the if-clause takes the present, will goes in the main clause.

ok.de: Richtig: If I were you gibt einen Rat → Hauptsatz mit would + Grundform: would check.
ok.en: Right: If I were you gives advice → main clause with would + base form: would check.

wrong.de: If I were you ist eine Annahme, kein echter Fall. Dann steht would, nicht will.
wrong.en: If I were you is an assumption, not a real case. Then would is used, not will.

wrong.de: would have checked blickt zurück. Der Rat gilt für jetzt, vor dem Unterschreiben.
wrong.en: would have checked looks back. The advice is for now, before signing.

wrong.de: Das Past allein wäre eine Tatsache. Im Hauptsatz einer Annahme steht would + Grundform.
wrong.en: The past alone would state a fact. The main clause of an assumption takes would + base form.

ok.de: Richtig: had known ist vorbei → would have + 3. Form: would have delayed.
ok.en: Right: had known (over) → would have + participle: would have delayed.

wrong.de: had known blickt zurück: Die Folge braucht would have + 3. Form.
wrong.en: had known looks back: the result needs would have + participle.

wrong.de: will meint Zukunft. Der Fehler ist aber längst bekannt, die Folge liegt in der Vergangenheit.
wrong.en: will points to the future. But the bug was known long ago, the result lies in the past.

wrong.de: Das einfache Past wäre eine Tatsache. Die unmögliche Folge braucht would have + 3. Form.
wrong.en: The simple past would state a fact. The impossible result needs would have + participle.

ok.de: Richtig: unless = „wenn nicht“ → Präsens ohne not: send.
ok.en: Right: unless = “if not” → present with no not: send.

wrong.de: Unless nennt eine mögliche Ausnahme: Danach steht das Präsens, nicht das Past.
wrong.en: Unless names a possible exception: the present follows, not the past.

wrong.de: Nach unless steht kein will, sondern das Präsens.
wrong.en: No will after unless, the present follows.

wrong.de: Doppelte Verneinung: unless heißt schon „wenn nicht“.
wrong.en: Double negation: unless already means “if not”.

ok.de: Richtig: provided that = vorausgesetzt, dass. Der Rabatt gilt nur bei 500 Stück.
ok.en: Right: provided that = on condition that. The discount applies only from 500 units.

wrong.de: in case = für den Fall, dass (Vorsorge). Hier geht es um eine Voraussetzung.
wrong.en: in case = as a precaution. Here it is a requirement.

wrong.de: whereas = während (Gegensatz) und nennt keine Bedingung.
wrong.en: whereas = while (contrast). It does not name a condition.

wrong.de: unless hieße „es sei denn“ und kehrt den Sinn um.
wrong.en: unless would mean “except if” and reverses the meaning.

ok.de: Richtig: would have baked (vorbei) → im if-Teil Past Perfect: had known.
ok.en: Right: would have baked (over) → the if-clause takes the Past Perfect: had known.

wrong.de: know ist Präsens. would have baked blickt zurück und braucht had + 3. Form.
wrong.en: know is present. would have baked looks back and needs had + participle.

wrong.de: knew wäre Second Conditional (jetzt). would have baked blickt zurück: had known.
wrong.en: knew would be second conditional (now). would have baked looks back: had known.

wrong.de: would steht nicht im if-Teil. Dort braucht Third Conditional had + 3. Form.
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The third conditional needs had + participle there.

ok.de: Richtig: reale Bedingung (today) → if + Präsens: sign. will steht im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: real condition (today) → if + present: sign. will goes in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach if steht kein will: Der if-Teil nimmt das Präsens (sign).
wrong.en: No will after if: the if-clause takes the present (sign).

wrong.de: would gehört nicht in den if-Teil. Hier reicht das Präsens (sign).
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The present (sign) is enough here.

wrong.de: Das Past macht es zur Annahme. Aber today nennt eine echte Möglichkeit.
wrong.en: The past makes it an assumption. But today names a real possibility.

wrong.de: Mit you steht sign ohne -s.
wrong.en: With you, sign takes no -s.

ok.de: Richtig: lowered = Annahme → Hauptsatz mit would + Grundform: would lose.
ok.en: Right: lowered = assumption → main clause with would + base form: would lose.

wrong.de: will passt nicht zu lowered. Eine Annahme verlangt would im Hauptsatz.
wrong.en: will does not fit lowered. An assumption calls for would in the main clause.

wrong.de: would have lost blickt zurück. Die Annahme gilt für jetzt: would lose.
wrong.en: would have lost looks back. The assumption is for now: would lose.

wrong.de: Die Folge einer Annahme braucht would + Grundform: would lose.
wrong.en: The result of an assumption needs would + base form: would lose.

ok.de: Richtig: at the time und last year → Past Perfect von have: had had.
ok.en: Right: at the time and last year → Past Perfect of have: had had.

wrong.de: would gehört nicht in den if-Teil. Dort steht had + 3. Form: had had.
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. It takes had + participle: had had.

wrong.de: Nach had steht die 3. Form von have: had had.
wrong.en: After had comes the participle of have: had had.

wrong.de: Die 3. Form von have ist had. Der if-Teil braucht deshalb had had.
wrong.en: The participle of have is had. So the if-clause needs had had.

wrong.de: Der if-Teil braucht Past Perfect (had + 3. Form), weil es um früher geht.
wrong.en: The if-clause needs the Past Perfect (had + participle) because it is about earlier.

ok.de: Richtig: Das ist eine feste Regel (automatically) → Präsens in beiden Teilen: registers.
ok.en: Right: fixed rule (automatically) → present in both parts: registers.

wrong.de: Eine feste Regel braucht das Präsens, kein will.
wrong.en: A fixed rule needs the present, not will.

wrong.de: would macht daraus eine Annahme. Hier gilt eine feste Regel.
wrong.en: would turns it into an assumption. Here a fixed rule applies.

wrong.de: Das Past macht es zur Annahme. automatically beschreibt eine feste Regel.
wrong.en: The past makes it an assumption. automatically describes a fixed rule.

wrong.de: Mit a customer braucht das Präsens ein -s: registers.
wrong.en: With a customer the present needs an -s: registers.

ok.de: Richtig: I'd be ist eine Annahme → if + Past, verneint didn't + Grundform: didn't spend.
ok.en: Right: I'd be = assumption → if + past, negative didn't + base form: didn't spend.

wrong.de: would gehört nicht in den if-Teil. Dort steht das Past (didn't spend).
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The past (didn't spend) goes there.

wrong.de: will gehört nicht in den if-Teil. I'd be zeigt eine Annahme: Past.
wrong.en: will does not go in the if-clause. I'd be signals an assumption: past.

wrong.de: Das Präsens wäre eine Tatsache. Die Annahme braucht das Past: didn't spend.
wrong.en: The present would state a fact. The assumption needs the past: didn't spend.

wrong.de: Nach didn't steht die Grundform: didn't spend, nicht spent.
wrong.en: After didn't comes the base form: didn't spend, not spent.

ok.de: Richtig: Der if-Teil dreht die Tatsache um: had prepared. Folge: wouldn't have lost.
ok.en: Right: the if-clause reverses the fact: had prepared. Result: wouldn't have lost.

wrong.de: would gehört nicht in den if-Teil. Dort braucht Third Conditional had + 3. Form.
wrong.en: would does not go in the if-clause. The third conditional needs had + participle there.

wrong.de: Der if-Teil dreht die Tatsache um: Ihr wart unvorbereitet, also had prepared ohne not.
wrong.en: The if-clause reverses the fact: you were unprepared, so had prepared with no not.

wrong.de: Nach had steht die 3. Form: had prepared.
wrong.en: After had comes the participle: had prepared.

wrong.de: Der if-Teil braucht Past Perfect: had prepared, nicht nur prepared.
wrong.en: The if-clause needs the Past Perfect: had prepared, not just prepared.

ok.de: Richtig: unless = „wenn nicht“ → Präsens ohne not: send.
ok.en: Right: unless = “if not” → present with no not: send.

wrong.de: Doppelte Verneinung: unless heißt schon „wenn nicht“, danach kein not.
wrong.en: Double negation: unless already means “if not”, so no not follows.

wrong.de: Nach unless steht kein will, sondern das Präsens.
wrong.en: No will after unless, the present follows.

wrong.de: Nach unless steht das Präsens, nicht das Past: send.
wrong.en: After unless the present follows, not the past: send.

ok.de: Richtig: Annahme → if + Past (had). would steht nur im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: assumption → if + past (had). would appears only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Das deutsche „würde haben“ wird im Englischen zu had: If we had more budget.
wrong.en: The German “würde haben” becomes had in English: If we had more budget.

wrong.de: Der if-Teil einer Annahme braucht das Past: had more budget.
wrong.en: The if-clause of an assumption needs the past: had more budget.

ok.de: Richtig: mögliche Zukunft → if + Präsens (agrees). will steht nur im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: possible future → if + present (agrees). will appears only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach if steht bei realer Zukunft das Präsens (agrees), will nur im Hauptsatz.
wrong.en: After if, a real future takes the present (agrees), will only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Das Verb im if-Teil muss ins Präsens: the client agrees (mit -s).
wrong.en: The verb in the if-clause must be present: the client agrees (with -s).

ok.de: Richtig: Annahme → if + Past (had). would steht nur im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: assumption → if + past (had). would appears only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Das deutsche „würde haben“ wird im Englischen zu had: If I had more money.
wrong.en: The German “würde haben” becomes had in English: If I had more money.

wrong.de: Der if-Teil einer Annahme braucht das Past: had more money.
wrong.en: The if-clause of an assumption needs the past: had more money.

ok.de: Richtig: mögliche Zukunft → if + Präsens (calls). will steht nur im Hauptsatz.
ok.en: Right: possible future → if + present (calls). will appears only in the main clause.

wrong.de: Nach if steht das Präsens (calls). will bleibt im Hauptsatz (I'll tell her).
wrong.en: After if the present follows (calls). will stays in the main clause (I'll tell her).

wrong.de: Im if-Teil braucht she das Präsens mit -s: calls.
wrong.en: In the if-clause she needs the present with -s: calls.

ok.de: Richtig: had left ist vorbei → would have + 3. Form: wouldn't have missed.
ok.en: Right: had left (over) → would have + participle: wouldn't have missed.

wrong.de: Nach had left liegt die Folge in der Vergangenheit: would not have missed.
wrong.en: After had left the result lies in the past: would not have missed.

wrong.de: Das have fehlt: Third Conditional = would have + 3. Form.
wrong.en: The have is missing: third conditional = would have + participle.
